'''Nomijinja''' (のみじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in Nomimachi, {{ill|Takatsuki|en|Takatsuki|qid=Q335423|lt=Takatsuki City}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|en|Osaka Prefecture|qid=Q122723|lt=Osaka Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} shrine, and its former Rank was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== History ==
In the late 9th century, during the mid-{{ill|Heian period|en|Heian period|qid=Q193292|lt=Heian period}} of {{ill|Emperor Uda|en|Emperor Uda|qid=Q349267|lt=Emperor Uda}} ({{ill|887|en|887|qid=Q25010|lt=887}} – {{ill|897|en|897|qid=Q30468|lt=897}}), an epidemic spread throughout the region. Following a divine oracle, {{ill|Gozu Tennō|de|Gozu-Tennō|it|Gozu Tennō|ja|牛頭天王|zh|牛頭天王|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozutennō}} (identified with {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}) was enshrined, and as the epidemic subsided, a shrine building was constructed, establishing the Gozutennō Shrine.

In the late 10th century, when {{ill|Takatsuki Castle|ja|高槻城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takatsuki Castle|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11670758}} was constructed, the shrine was venerated as a guardian of the castle.<ref name=nomijinja>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.nomijinja.jp/ |title=高槻城内守護 野見神社 |publisher=野見神社 |accessdate=2014-12-13}}</ref> However, in the 16th century when {{ill|Justo Takayama|en|Justo Takayama|qid=Q749873|lt=Takayama Ukon}} became the lord of Takatsuki Castle, his adherence to {{ill|Christianity|en|Christianity|qid=Q5043|lt=Christianity}} led him to destroy the shrine building within the castle and confiscate its estate. Later, in the 5th year of the {{ill|Yuanhe|en|Yuanhe|qid=Q10889567|lt=Genna}} era ({{ill|1619|en|1619|qid=Q6804|lt=1619}}), the lord of Takatsuki Castle, {{ill|Matsudaira Ienobu|en|Matsudaira Ienobu|qid=Q5368670|lt=Matsudaira Ienobu}}, rebuilt the shrine building.<ref name=nomi_history>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.nomijinja.jp/%e5%be%a1%e7%94%b1%e7%b7%92-%e8%a1%8c%e4%ba%8b.html |title=野見神社 御由緒・年間行事 |publisher=野見神社 |accessdate=2014-12-13}}</ref>

bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Separation of Shinto and Buddhism}}, the name of the enshrined deity was changed to {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, and furthermore, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|de|Nomi-no-Sukune|fa|نومی نو سوکونه|ff|Nomi no Sukune|fr|Nomi-no-Sukune|ja|野見宿禰|ru|Номи-но Сукунэ|uk|Номі-но-Сукуне|zh|野見宿禰|qid=Q965742|lt=Nomitatsune-no-Mikoto}} was enshrined alongside, prompting the shrine to be renamed “Nomijinja”. Consequently, although it is counted as one of the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}} shrines listed in the {{ill|Engi Shiki Shinmei-chō|ja|延喜式神名帳}}, the publication “Historic Sites, Famous Landscapes, and Natural Monuments of Osaka Prefecture” asserts that the renaming to “Nomijinja”—by enshrining Nomitatsune to emulate a Shikinaisha—meant that its descendant shrine is the auxiliary shrine {{ill|Nomigami Shrine|ja|野身神社}} of {{ill|Jōgū Tenmangū|ja|上宮天満宮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamigu Tenmangu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11358789}} in Takatsuki City.

In {{ill|1871|en|1871|qid=Q7746|lt=1871}} (the 4th year of Meiji), it was classified as a prefectural shrine ({{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}) as a Shikinaisha; however, in November of the following year, {{ill|1872|en|1872|qid=Q7753|lt=1872}} (the 5th year of Meiji), it was demoted to a village shrine ({{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}) for the reasons mentioned above.

== Enshrined Deities ==
* Main Deities – {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|de|Nomi-no-Sukune|fa|نومی نو سوکونه|ff|Nomi no Sukune|fr|Nomi-no-Sukune|ja|野見宿禰|ru|Номи-но Сукунэ|uk|Номі-но-Сукуне|zh|野見宿禰|qid=Q965742|lt=Nomitatsune-no-Mikoto}}

== Shrine Grounds ==
=== Shrine Buildings ===
* Main Hall – Rebuilt in the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenna|en|Tenna|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenwa}} ({{ill|1682|en|1682|qid=Q7648|lt=1682}}).
* Haiden – Renovated in {{ill|2003|en|2003|qid=Q1986|lt=2003}} (the 15th year of {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}).
* Noh Stage
* Shrine Office

=== Auxiliary Shrines ===
* {{ill|Nomi Shrine (Q11646130)|ja|永井神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 野見神社 (高槻市)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11646130}} – Enshrined deity: the first lord of {{ill|Takatsuki Domain|en|Takatsuki Domain|qid=Q10863415|lt=Takatsuki Domain}}, {{ill|Nagai Naokiyo|ja|永井直清|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naotoki|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549807}}. Founded in the 5th year of the {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} era ({{ill|1793|en|1793|qid=Q7807|lt=1793}}) by the 9th lord, {{ill|Nagai Naonobu|ja|永井直進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naotoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549817}}. Initially called “Naotoki Shrine”, it was referred to as “Naotoki Gongen” during the late Edo period. In the first year of the {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei}} era ({{ill|1848|en|1848|qid=Q7647|lt=1848}}), during the time of the 11th lord, {{ill|Nagai Naoteru|ja|永井直輝|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naoteru|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549816}}, the main hall (a designated tangible cultural property of Takatsuki City) was restored, and the haiden (also a designated tangible cultural property) along with the karamon (quadrangular gate, designated tangible cultural property) were established. The karamon was repaired in {{ill|2010|en|2010|qid=Q1995|lt=2010}} (the 22nd year of {{ill|Heisei era|en|Heisei era|qid=Q234510|lt=Heisei}}).  
: Annual Festival: April 24<ref name=nomi_setsumatsu>{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.nomijinja.jp/%e6%91%82%e6%9c%ab%e7%a4%be.html |title=野見神社 - 摂末社 |publisher=野見神社 |accessdate=2014-12-13}}</ref>
* {{ill|Kojima Shrine|ja|小島神社}} – Enshrined deities: {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|市杵島姫命|lt=Ichikishima-hime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大己貴命|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=おほなむちのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi|qid=Q276944}}, {{ill|Iwanaga-hime|ja|磐長姫命|lt=Iwanagahime-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=いわながひめのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwanagahime|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to イワナガヒメ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q8191705}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|ja|天児屋根命|lt=Ameno Koyane-no-Mikoto|lt_ja=あめのこやねのみこと|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ameno Koyane|qid=Q2564508|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q2564508}}. Its founding date is unknown; the shrine building was newly constructed on October 1, {{ill|2021|en|2021|qid=Q49628|lt=2021}} (the 3rd year of {{ill|Reiwa era|en|Reiwa era|qid=Q62609017|lt=Reiwa}}).  
: Annual Festival: Second Sunday of October (Nomijinja Autumn Evening Festival)
* Shishamyojin – In the {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō period}} the separate shrines of Fukujinja, Inari Shrine, Iwajinsha, and Sorei Shrine were merged into one.  
: Annual Festival: April 11  
:: Fukujinja – Enshrined deities: {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|ja|志那都比古神|lt=Shinatsuhikokami|lt_ja=しなつひこのかみ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinatsuhikokami|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to シナツヒコ|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1073925}}, {{ill|Shinatsuhime|ja|志那都姫神|lt=Shinatsuhime}}, {{ill|Kagu-tsuchi|ja|火産霊|lt=Homusubi}}, {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|ja|金山比古神|lt=Kanayamahikokami}}, {{ill|Kanayama-hiko and Kanayama-hime|ja|金山姫神|lt=Kanayamahime}}, {{ill|Haniyamahikokami|ja|埴山比古神|lt=Haniyamahikokami}} (linked as {{ill|Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|it|Haniyasu|ja|ハニヤス|pl|Haniyasu|zh|波邇夜須毘古神與波邇夜須毘賣神|qid=Q9285919|lt=Haniyamas}} with display 埴山比古神), and {{ill|Mizuhanome|it|Mizuhanome|ja|ミヅハノメ|pl|Mizuhanome|sv|Mizuhanome|zh|彌都波能賣神|qid=Q8191796|lt=Mizuhanomenokami}}. Founded in August of the 9th year of {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} ({{ill|1797|en|1797|qid=Q7820|lt=1797}}) by {{ill|Nagai Naonobu|ja|永井直進|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagai Naotoshi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11549817}}.  
:: Inari Shrine – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ukanomitama|en|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukano Mitama-no-Kami}}. Founded in February of the 11th year of Kansei ({{ill|1799|en|1799|qid=Q7827|lt=1799}}) by Nagai Naotoshi.  
:: Iwajinsha – Enshrined deities: (i) Yachimata Hikonami, (ii) Yachimata Hime, and (iii) Kunado-no-Kami. Founded in May of the 4th year of {{ill|Genbun|de|Genbun|fa|گنبون|fr|Ère Genbun|ja|元文|ko|겐분|ru|Гэмбун|simple|Genbun|sr|Генбун|sv|Genbun|tr|Genbun|zh|元文 (日本)|qid=Q1145754|lt=Genbun}} ({{ill|1739|en|1739|qid=Q7002|lt=1739}}) by {{ill|Nagai Ryunosuke|ja|永井流之助}}.  
:: Sorei Shrine – Enshrined are the successive chief priests, shrine priests, and parishioners who have devoted themselves to the shrine. Founded in {{ill|1878|en|1878|qid=Q7776|lt=1878}} (the 11th year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}).
* {{ill|Takatsuki Ebisu Shrine|ja|高槻えびす神社}} – Enshrined deity: {{ill|Ebisu|ja|蛭子大神}}. It was established in {{ill|1956|en|1956|qid=Q5221|lt=1956}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa}} 31) as a branch from {{ill|Nishinomiya Shrine|en|Nishinomiya Shrine|qid=Q705297|lt=Nishinomiya Shrine}}, and the current shrine building was constructed in {{ill|1966|en|1966|qid=Q2649|lt=1966}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Showa}} 41).  
: Takatsuki Ebisu Festival – January 10 (subdivided into the 9th: Evening Ebisu, 10th: Main Ebisu, 11th: Remaining Fortune)
* {{ill|Gokoku Shrines|en|Gokoku shrines|qid=Q1534477|lt=Gokoku Shrine}} – Enshrined are the war dead of Takatsuki who perished in the {{ill|Satsuma Rebellion|en|Satsuma Rebellion|qid=Q714820|lt=Satsuma Rebellion}}, {{ill|First Sino-Japanese War|en|First Sino-Japanese War|qid=Q178687|lt=First Sino-Japanese War}}, {{ill|Russo-Japanese War|en|Russo-Japanese War|qid=Q159950|lt=Russo-Japanese War}}, {{ill|Second Sino-Japanese War|en|Second Sino-Japanese War|qid=Q170314|lt=Second Sino-Japanese War}}, and the {{ill|Pacific War|en|Pacific War|qid=Q184425|lt=Pacific War}}.  
: Annual Festival: Third Sunday of May<ref name=nomi_setsumatsu/>
